gaps.sentence: By the age of thirty, she ___ her own company.
gaps.hint: by the age of means completed before
gaps.explanation: An achievement completed before a past reference point takes the past perfect: had started.

gaps.sentence: Shakespeare ___ thirty-seven plays that we know of.
gaps.hint: a dead historical figure, finished lifetime
gaps.explanation: Actions of people who are no longer alive take the past simple even without a time phrase: wrote.

gaps.sentence: She ___ two majors when she was at university.
gaps.hint: a completed period in the past
gaps.explanation: A completed past period takes the past simple: did.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ a lot since the new road opened.
gaps.hint: since clause with a present result
gaps.explanation: Change that started in the past and continues to now takes the present perfect: has changed.

gaps.sentence: Who ___ this bag belong to? It has been sitting here all morning.
gaps.hint: the question form needs auxiliary does
gaps.explanation: Present simple questions need the auxiliary 'does' plus the base verb: does this bag belong to.

gaps.sentence: This time tomorrow I ___ my driving test.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future time takes the future continuous: will be taking.

gaps.sentence: I ___ you were coming today — nobody told me!
gaps.hint: state verb forbids the past continuous
gaps.explanation: 'Know' is a state verb, so its past form is the past simple: didn't know.

gaps.sentence: I ___ it matters whether we leave at six or seven — the traffic will be terrible either way.
gaps.hint: think meaning believe is a state verb
gaps.explanation: 'Think' in the sense of 'believe' is a state verb, so the negative present simple is used: don't think.
